stem:
Tanya pours seawater into a wide open pan and gently heats it on a stove until no liquid remains. She wants the dry dissolved salt left behind.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: When the water evaporates completely, the dissolved salt is left as a solid in the pan.
Dry salt is recovered as soon as the seawater feels warm, even if liquid remains.
This single heating step alone also collects a jug of pure liquid water with the dry salt.
The salt returns only if the seawater boils with large bubbles; quiet warming cannot work.

teacher.key_rationale: Evaporation removes water and leaves dissolved salt. Warmth alone without loss of water is not enough; collecting pure liquid water needs a separate condensation step; bubbles are not required.
